reviewer: Fable 349a plan review (D4 approved); owner policy
review: security Go bug fixed in Rust
reason: Go's postAuth treats forgot-password/begin's 200 decoy as a successful authentication and clears ip:/user:/ip_user: lockout keys, so four wrong passwords plus one begin call reset the counter indefinitely. Rust writes Go's success attempt row but never clears lockout keys for this response.

reviewer: Fable 349a plan review F1; owner policy
review: security Go bug fixed in Rust
reason: Go derives the lockout/spray username with a whole-body json.Unmarshal while handlers accept trailing data, so `{...} x` authenticated with an empty username: no lockout check, no escalation, spray blind. Rust uses each route handler's own first-value decode (login ingress::Login; forgot-password and guest-invite ingress::fields email).

reviewer: Fable 349a plan review F1; owner policy
review: security Go bug fixed in Rust (HTTP only)
reason: Go skips the lockout step when the username is empty. HTTP admission checks the ip: key alone in that case, so a spray-armed ip: lock always applies.

reviewer: Fable 349a plan review F2; owner policy
review: security Go bug fixed in Rust
reason: Go keys /auth/refresh on the body email field or the unverified JWT email, so {"email":victim,"refresh_token":<own valid token>} clears the victim's lockout and forged JWTs escalate any account. Rust keys only the email claim of a refresh token that verifies; otherwise only the ip: key is checked.

review: security Go bug fixed in Rust
reason: Go's captcha token is unbound and reusable for 120 s. Rust's MAC binds answer|exp|source IP|route|username (digits-only answer and exp). A verified token is claimed once per auth process, only after the pipeline allows the request, in a bounded in-memory used set (65 536 entries; full refuses). A restart empties the set, so a token accepted before a restart is accepted once more within its remaining 120 s (still bound to IP, route and username); with several auth processes a token is accepted once per process (production runs one).

review: security Go bug fixed in Rust
reason: Go answers a failed token before the pipeline, so failed checks are never rate limited or tarpitted. Rust runs the pipeline first (tarpit, rate limit, lockout, spray; no captcha threshold); its refusal wins, otherwise 403 CAPTCHA verification failed. A failed single-use claim counts as a failed token. A verified, claimed token runs Go's skip step.
Go derives the captcha key from JWT_SECRET even when empty (a public key). Rust derives only from a non-empty secret; otherwise the key is empty and every solve fails.
An AuthServer without a Gate answers 503 'threat admission unavailable' on every credential route instead of serving it unadmitted.

HTTP maps ip_rules_unavailable, lockout_unavailable, spray_unavailable, rate_limit_unavailable and captcha_unavailable to 403 'Access denied by security policy' with no attempt row and no handler; Go proceeds.
